research.name: The Kempner Institute at Harvard University
highlights: Supporting an institute project to build biologically-constrained computational models of the mouse brain

Developed a reproducible and highly configurable set of randomly generated simulation environments that allow research questions to be answered quickly e.g. Does the agent's visual-spatial mapping generalize across lighting conditions?
Investigating the capabilities and limitations of reinforcement learning-based action selection using representations from a biologically plausible cortico-hippocampal circuit
Investigating whether confidence in a biologically inspired visual-spatial mapping circuit can guide exploration through intrinsic motivation
Core contributor to a NeuroAI research platform supporting composable neural circuits with heterogeneous learning rules

research.name: Los Alamos National Laboratory
research.position: Robotics and Automation Rapid Prototype Intern
highlights: Collaboratively designed, built, and programmed a robotic system for autonomous assembly and disassembly of DPP-3 shipping containers for radioactive material
Led the computer vision aspect of the project, fine-tuning pre-trained neural networks to recognize bolts and report their location in the camera frame
Presented design in a conference publication and talk at Waste Management Symposium 2025

research.name: The University of Tennessee Oak Ridge Innovation Institute
research.position: Student Mentoring and Research Training Intern
highlights: Studied the tradeoff between computational cost and generated path quality across two models of quadrotor dynamics in MATLAB simulations with the GPOPS-II optimizer

Found the simpler model used less compute and generated more optimal paths, but noted that imprecision in the physical model of the quadrotor must be addressed before a final determination can be made
Presented findings with a poster and talk at an end-of-program symposium

projects.name: Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Quadruped Jumping
highlights: Extended an existing PyTorch-based quadruped locomotion project in NVIDIA IsaacSim by introducing flying obstacles and using reward-shaping to teach the quadruped to jump over them
Designed a two-stage curriculum: stage I focused on achieving ideal jumping motion, while stage II integrated dynamic obstacles

projects.name: Speedrunning the Boston MBTA
highlights: Formulated a relaxed traveling salesman problem using public transit travel times and pedestrian connections to minimize the time required to visit all 125 MBTA rail stations
Completed the route in 8 hours and 31 minutes and coauthored an interactive article documenting the methodology and expedition
